data.name: drug_interaction_rules
rows: Do not prescribe both together unless there is a clear justification.
The combination may increase QT prolongation risk.
Avoid the combination and consider an alternative antibiotic.
This duplicates proton pump inhibitor therapy.
Use only one proton pump inhibitor at a time.
Use only one antihistamine to reduce excess sedation.
The combination can increase hypoglycemia risk.
Monitor blood glucose and counsel the patient on hypoglycemia symptoms.
Diclofenac can substantially increase bleeding risk when used with Warfarin.
Avoid the combination; consider Paracetamol if analgesia is needed.
Azithromycin may increase Atorvastatin exposure in susceptible patients.
Monitor for muscle pain and consider holding the statin during short antibiotic courses.
Prednisolone can worsen glycemic control in patients taking Metformin.
Monitor blood glucose during corticosteroid treatment.
Loperamide may mask symptoms in infectious diarrhea while rehydration is ongoing.
Assess the cause of diarrhea and prioritize rehydration.
Aspirin increases bleeding risk when used with Warfarin.
Avoid the combination when possible; if both are required, monitor INR and bleeding closely.
Ibuprofen increases bleeding risk when used with Warfarin.
Avoid NSAIDs when possible; consider Paracetamol and monitor INR closely.
Clarithromycin can sharply increase Simvastatin exposure and rhabdomyolysis risk.
Do not combine; choose another antibiotic or temporarily stop Simvastatin.
Gemfibrozil markedly increases Simvastatin toxicity risk.
Do not combine; consider another lipid-lowering strategy.
Amiodarone can increase Simvastatin exposure and muscle toxicity.
Limit Simvastatin dose or switch to a lower-interaction statin.
Combining Sildenafil with nitrates can cause profound hypotension.
Contraindicated; avoid Sildenafil within 24 to 48 hours of nitrate use.
Trimethoprim increases bone marrow suppression risk with Methotrexate.
Do not combine; use another antibiotic and monitor blood counts.
Furosemide-induced hypokalemia can increase Digoxin toxicity.
Monitor potassium and Digoxin levels and replace potassium if needed.
Ciprofloxacin can greatly increase Tizanidine exposure.
Do not combine; select another antibiotic.
Ciprofloxacin can raise Theophylline concentration and toxicity risk.
Reduce Theophylline dose and monitor levels if coadministration is unavoidable.
NSAIDs can reduce Lithium clearance and increase toxicity.
Avoid the combination or monitor Lithium closely.
The combination may increase hyperkalemia risk.
Monitor serum potassium and limit supplementation unless necessary.
Prolonged high-dose Paracetamol may increase INR in patients taking Warfarin.
Use the lowest effective Paracetamol dose and monitor INR.
The combination may increase serotonin syndrome and seizure risk.
Avoid the combination; consider another analgesic.
Omeprazole may reduce Clopidogrel activation through CYP2C19 inhibition.
Prefer Pantoprazole or another lower-interaction acid suppressor.
Dual antihistamine therapy may increase sedation.
Advise patients to monitor drowsiness and avoid driving if sedated.
